clue.text: Obliging with a fine story

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
a fable is a short moral story

explanation.surface: Someone helpful turns up with a good yarn to tell.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obliging is friendly and easy to deal with, the sense of the synonym affable.

clue.text: Outsiders ignored late invite for bash

indicators.note: the outside letters of the word late are left out, keeping its middle

parts.note: to tempt is to invite or entice

explanation.surface: Gatecrashers were overlooked when a late invitation went out for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bash' looks like a party, fitting the invite, but it means a go: have a bash.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a bash at something is to have a try, so bash is an attempt.

clue.text: Approving Hitchcock's work is contemptible

parts.note: to be for something is to approve of it
The Birds is a 1963 Alfred Hitchcock film

explanation.surface: Praising a director's film turns out to be despicable.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for the birds describes something worthless, deserving contempt.

clue.text: Game that may involve suspension

definitions.meaning: a card game for four players

explanation.surface: A sport in which a player might be banned.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge is a card game, and a suspension bridge is one kind of crossing.

clue.text: After gin, fell over in hub of activity

parts.note: a gin is a machine, such as a cotton gin; the word is short for engine

indicators.note: over means the word for fell is turned backwards

parts.note: a fell is upland moor in northern England

explanation.surface: A drinker topples over in a busy place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' reads as the drink, and 'fell' as fell down; both are nouns. 'After' only says the moor part comes later.
explanation.definitionFit: The engine room powers a ship, so figuratively it is the centre of activity.

clue.text: City lacking it, campaign for tree

indicators.note: lacking says the word that follows is taken away from the city

parts.note: to press is to campaign or push hard for something

explanation.surface: A town without something launches a drive on behalf of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The cypress is an evergreen conifer, so the clue names it by its general class.

clue.text: From country, small piece forcibly removed

definitions.meaning: a landlocked nation of north-central Africa
the bit of paper punched out of a card or ballot

explanation.surface: A fragment torn from a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Chad is an African nation, and a chad is a punched-out scrap, famous from the 2000 Florida ballots.

clue.text: Insolence between two Greek characters in battle

indicators.note: between says the insolence word sits inside the pair of letters

parts.note: phi and pi are two letters of the Greek alphabet
the second of the two Greek letters is pi
lip is cheek or insolence

explanation.surface: Rudeness between a couple of Greeks breaks out into a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Philippi was the site of the 42 BC battle where Antony and Octavian defeated Brutus and Cassius.

clue.text: Ring-tailed creature has no hands: it can't get off the ground

definitions.text: it can't get off the ground

indicators.note: the two hands are left and right, so L and R are taken out

parts.note: the ring-tailed lemur of Madagascar

explanation.surface: A primate without hands is grounded.
explanation.walkthrough: L and R stand for left and right, the two hands.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a flightless Australian bird, so it never gets airborne.

clue.text: Southern sky less hot: put this on?

indicators.note: less says the hot letter is taken away

parts.note: the sky stands for the weather, what it is doing overhead
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: With the southern skies cooling, wrap up warm.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole picture: when it is less hot, you put this on.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweater is a jumper, a knitted garment pulled on when it turns chilly.

clue.text: Height of party cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the party word loses its final letter

parts.note: the Tory party is Britain's Conservative party

explanation.surface: How tall a political group stands once it has been trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tor is a rocky hill or peak, especially on Dartmoor, so a height.

clue.text: Intrigued at extraordinarily base behaviour

indicators.note: something done extraordinarily is out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is fascinated by a show of unusually low conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinarily' looks like it goes with 'base', but it is the anagram signal on INTRIGUED AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Failing to show thanks is a mean, low kind of conduct, so base behaviour.

clue.text: Wooden hut in spring

indicators.note: in says the hut word sits inside the spring month

parts.note: May is a month of spring
a hogan is a traditional Navajo dwelling, a hut of logs and earth

explanation.surface: A timber shack in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahogany is a hardwood, so something made of it is wooden.

clue.text: Ring little bird, say

indicators.note: say tells us the young bird's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a cygnet is a young swan

explanation.surface: A request to phone a small feathered friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a verb, as in phone, but it is the noun: a signet ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A signet is a seal ring, worn on the finger and pressed into wax.

clue.text: We never say energy's failed when it's party time

indicators.note: something that has failed has broken down, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: We never admit our energy ran out when it's time to celebrate.
explanation.definitionFit: The last night of December is the classic occasion for celebrating.

clue.text: Dreadful flak — I eject in this?

definitions.text: Dreadful flak — I eject in this?

indicators.note: dreadful signals a mess, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pilot under terrible fire bails out wearing protective gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot ejecting over the sea wears a buoyant vest to stay afloat, a life jacket.

clue.text: Play about black man in jug

indicators.note: about says the play word goes round the letter for black

parts.note: to toy is to play idly
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A drama about a dark figure locked in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jug' suggests prison slang, but it is a pottery jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A Toby jug is a beer mug shaped like a seated man in a tricorn hat.

clue.text: Supporter running government intelligence

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment that gives support
a party running the government is in power

explanation.surface: A backer of the ruling regime supplies secret information.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainpower means mental ability, which is what intelligence means here.

clue.text: Shortest line gets halved: poem meant to be written like that

indicators.note: halved keeps the first half of the word gets

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

parts.words: meant to be written like that
parts.note: sic is the Latin note saying a quotation is reproduced exactly

explanation.surface: A line is cut short, and the poem is printed that way on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A geodesic is the shortest path between two points on a curved surface.

clue.text: Ensure new job is fixed up for painter

indicators.note: fixed up means put together again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to make sure a decorator gets the work arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Burne-Jones was a Victorian Pre-Raphaelite painter and designer.

clue.text: Outstanding performance as Cornwall, as against Gloucester

definitions.meaning: British slang for a brilliant display
in King Lear the Duke of Cornwall puts out the Earl of Gloucester's eyes

explanation.surface: A standout game by one county side against another.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall and Gloucester read as English counties playing a match, but they are characters in King Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: A blinder is a superb performance, and also one who blinds, as Cornwall does Gloucester.

clue.text: Needing to replace energy, concocted sweet drink

indicators.note: to replace means the energy letter is put back in another place

parts.note: something concocted has been made
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A brewer who has run out of steam knocks up a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Mead is an old drink fermented from honey, so a sweet drink.

clue.text: 'As encyclopaedist gone off?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, "'As encyclopaedist gone off? (7)", opens with a stray quote mark and appears cut short; the scan does not show it and no search found the rest, so the wordplay for DIDEROT cannot be parsed.

clue.text: Crack around dry bed

indicators.note: around says the crack word goes round the dry letters

parts.note: a boom is a loud crack of sound
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: Fissures spread across a parched riverbed.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom of a river or sea is its bed.

clue.text: Imprisoned, having done such a job?

definitions.meaning: a crime done with help from within

explanation.surface: Someone is locked up for a crime committed by an employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside is slang for in prison, and an inside job is a crime by an insider.

clue.text: Frowned over a book that's stilted

indicators.note: over says the frowning word covers the other letters, which go inside it

parts.note: to lour is to frown or scowl

explanation.surface: Someone scowled over a volume with stiff prose.
explanation.definitionFit: Laboured writing shows its effort and is forced, the sense of stilted.

clue.text: Briefly raise a narcotic

indicators.note: briefly means the raise word loses its last letter

parts.note: to cock is to raise, as one cocks an eyebrow

explanation.surface: Quickly lift a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Coca is the South American shrub whose leaves yield cocaine, a narcotic.

clue.text: Weld rectory desk that's broken

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: A welder is told to fix a vicar's damaged desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weld' looks like a metalworking verb, but it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Weld is a plant once grown for its yellow dye, also called dyer's rocket.

clue.text: Drop of water

parts.note: not a droplet but the falling away of the sea as the tide goes out

explanation.definitionFit: The ebb is the outflow of the tide, when the water level falls.

clue.text: Bit of corn one hears

definitions.meaning: the seed-bearing head of a cereal plant

explanation.surface: A piece of maize is something people listen with.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of corn and the organ of hearing share one spelling.

clue.text: Maxim she betrayed/—- she loved Ivanhoe

definitions.meaning: in Daphne du Maurier's novel the first wife of Maxim de Winter was unfaithful to him
in Scott's Ivanhoe the Jewish heroine loves the knight

explanation.surface: A woman who was unfaithful to one man and devoted to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maxim' looks like a saying, but it is a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Two literary heroines share the name: du Maurier's title character and Scott's heroine.

clue.text: Outburst from one briefly engaged is in French

parts.note: a temp is a worker hired for a short time
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A short-term worker has an outburst in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm, and figuratively an outburst of emotion.
